definitions.explanation: The perspective of viewing things from outside oneself, without personal bias or emotional involvement. Contrasts with subjectivity.

examples.japanese: {客観|きゃっかん}が{大切|たいせつ}だ。
{客観|きゃっかん}と{主観|しゅかん}のバランスを{取|と}る。
examples.english: To strike a balance between objectivity and subjectivity.

examples.japanese: {物事|ものごと}を{客観|きゃっかん}で{見|み}ることは{簡単|かんたん}ではない。
examples.english: It is not easy to view things from an objective standpoint.

examples.japanese: {研究者|けんきゅうしゃ}には{客観|きゃっかん}に{基|もと}づいた{分析|ぶんせき}が{求|もと}められる。
examples.english: Researchers are expected to provide analysis grounded in objectivity.

notes:
Refers to the standpoint of evaluating or observing things impartially, without personal feelings or prejudice. Frequently appears in academic, journalistic, and philosophical contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {客観|きゃっかん}的（な）: objective (adjective form, extremely common)
- {客観|きゃっかん}的に{見|み}る: to look at objectively
- {客観|きゃっかん}的{事実|じじつ}: objective fact
- {客観|きゃっかん}性（を{保|たも}つ）: objectivity (to maintain objectivity)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {主観|しゅかん}: subjectivity — the direct opposite; personal, subjective viewpoint
- {中立|ちゅうりつ}: neutrality — not taking sides, but not necessarily the same as being objective
- {公正|こうせい}: fairness — emphasizes impartial treatment, often in legal or institutional contexts

FORMS:
{客|きゃく} (guest, outsider) + {観|かん} (view) — literally "viewing as an outsider," i.e., seeing from a detached perspective.
